title: Word order with eikö with plural owners
summary: Build plural-owner negative questions: eikö + owner + ole + partitive thing.
prerequisiteSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
objectives: Build plural-owner negative questions: eikö + owner + ole + partitive thing.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Build plural-owner negative questions: eikö + owner + ole + partitive thing.
Put meillä, teillä, and heillä immediately after eikö. Keep ole separate, after the owner, then finish with the complete partitive noun.
keyPoints: Build plural-owner negative questions: eikö + owner + ole + partitive thing.

steps: Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put meillä next. meillä means “we as the owner”.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive koiraa (“a dog”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put teillä next. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive kirjaa (“a book”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put heillä next. heillä means “they as the owner”.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive kissaa (“a cat”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put teillä next. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive tyynyä (“a pillow”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
meillä identifies the plural owner in this word order with eikö with plural owners pattern.
Use Eikö + owner + ole; the negative question keeps this fixed verb pattern.
kynää (“a pen”) is the complete regular singular partitive: kynä + -ä.
teillä identifies the plural owner in this word order with eikö with plural owners pattern.
Use Eikö + owner + ole; the negative question keeps this fixed verb pattern.
peliä (“a game”) is the complete regular singular partitive: peli + -ä.

commonMistakes: Keep the requested order Eikö + owner + ole + partitive noun; the owner goes between Eikö and ole.
Do not lose ole or the noun ending while arranging the question.

parts.formation: Ei + the question ending -kö = eikö. The front-vowel ending follows ei, independently of the noun.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: he has the learned possession form heillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Negative possession keeps ole after eikö, with every owner.
pallo + -a = palloa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.
